title: Backcompat contracts and automated rollout validators across runtime, API, SDKs, Console
creator: Priya Natarajan
description: Goal: Define machine-readable backwards-compatibility contracts per product surface (runtime, public API, SDKs, Console) and implement a set of automated rollout validators that run as pre-flight checks in CI and as runtime canary guards. This ticket covers the contract schema, the validator rules, a CLI pre-flight tool (redwood-upgrade-check), and CI/console integration for gating upgrades on Dedicated/Private/Hosted channels.
acceptance_criteria: A1: A single canonical contract schema (YAML) exists and describes compatibility expectations for: runtime, REST API, SDKs (py/js/go), Console UI. Schema stored under //docs/release/contracts/backcompat.yaml
A2: redwood-upgrade-check CLI validates an artifact bundle against the contract and returns non-zero on breaking changes. CLI integration added to runtime/ci and sdk/ci pipelines
A3: rollout-validator CI job added to release pipelines that runs against a representative test matrix (short E2E prompts, schema compat tests, kv/cache sanity for runtime)
A4: Console shows gating status and last validation run for any channel rollout (Hosted/Dedicated/Private) with a link to failing CI logs
A5: A small canary rollout (5% traffic) will be automatically blocked if validators detect major API or runtime regressions; block rules and thresholds documented
A6: Documentation and runbook for on-call to troubleshoot blocked rollouts and perform emergency rollbacks
plan: Design contract schema and compatibility levels (compatibility_levels: stable, soft-breaking, hard-breaking, experimental)
Implement contract generator that extracts public API surface from OpenAPI + SDK introspection + runtime capability manifest
Prototype redwood-upgrade-check CLI (python) that compares new artifact against baseline contract and runs a light compatibility suite
Add rollout-validator job to CI templates for runtime and SDK repos; wire job outputs to release dashboard
Integrate validator status into Console rollouts page and add a link from Dedicated control-plane UI
Run a pilot release against runtime-2.0 branch with internal teams and iterate on false-positive tuning
decisions: Semantic versioning policy: use semver for public API and SDKs; runtime follows release channels with a documented mapping to semver-like compatibility flags

Compatibility levels chosen: stable (no behavior or schema changes), soft-breaking (opt-in changes or additions with feature flags), hard-breaking (incompatible change requiring coordinated upgrade), experimental (no guarantees)

Validators will be conservative by default (favor blocking) and will expose a strictness toggle per release channel (e.g., Hosted default strict=true, Dedicated can opt strict=false for internal rollouts)
We will not attempt binary-level compatibility checks for all third-party kernels; instead runtime will publish a capability manifest used by contracts
risks: False positives in validators could unnecessarily block safe rollouts and increase friction
Maintaining contract generator across multiple SDK languages may drift if SDK maintainers don't keep introspection metadata up to date
Performance-sensitive runtime changes might pass API compatibility but still degrade latency SLA; validators need runtime perf smoke tests
Overly prescriptive contracts could slow down urgent security or critical fixes if rollback paths aren't clear
